name: Qwen Flash-Next
summary: Qwen's experimental 125B-A6B hybrid-attention MoE. Its 51B n-gram embedding enables selective host placement, and the official FP8 export now serves cache-zero text across the complete configured-512 MTP0-4 depth grid on four B70s. MTP4 reached a 20.727 tok/s short-screen decode median. At exact 4K, 32-block MTP1 and MTP2 recipes passed at 8.904 and 9.893 tok/s decode; MTP3 remains preferred at 15.502 tok/s decode, 187.9 seconds TTFT, and 1.246 tok/s wall output. Bounded MTP1 active-1K and active-2K arms both stopped on their first requests with no output; the 2K arm reached its 360-second client bound, the engine then reported its own timeout, and the post-failure teardown window recorded resets of both engine classes on all four cards before device rediscovery. Separate MTP2 and MTP3 active-2K requests completed their generic exact-depth gates but diverged from the frozen MTP0 token array at generated tokens 13 and five; both diagnostic rates receive no speed or quality credit and those cells are quarantined. MTP4 remains quarantined at exact 4K. Deterministic direct-answer quality is 6/7 semantically, while the separate official-thinking target profile passed 25/25. The MTP3 transfer completed and matched MTP0 on 19 required rows before the repeated-session boundary stopped the remaining six, so MTP thinking parity at depth 3 and deployment stability remain inconclusive and unqualified.

b70_fit.basis: The exact FP8 export became healthy and served real text requests on all four cards.

quality_evidence.scope: The deterministic direct-answer target profile is 6/7 semantically: the case-only logic output is correct, while the code expression remains wrong. A separate official-thinking MTP0 target profile passed a 4/4 scout and 21/21 three-seed grid with separated reasoning/final fields, normal stops, complete usage, and zero cache reuse. MTP0 also passed screened 1K/2K/4K and formal 8K gates; TP4 MTP1-4 at configured 512 are separate matched-quality cells. MTP4 matched all 26 bounded MTP0 outputs, passed 16/16 repeats and the small needle, accepted 1,716/1,716 cumulative draft tokens, and measured a 20.727 tok/s short-screen median. At configured 4352, 32-block MTP1 and MTP2 recipes each matched all 26 sealed MTP0 comparisons, passed 16/16 repeats, the exact 4K needle, a formal p4096/o128 gate, and all three p4096/o256 rows. MTP2 measured 9.893 tok/s decode, 263.3 seconds TTFT, and 0.891 tok/s wall output; the earlier 21-block stop is retained as superseded history. TP4/MTP3 remains the preferred exact-4K recipe at 15.502 tok/s decode, 187.9 seconds TTFT, and 1.246 tok/s wall output. Its official-thinking transfer completed 19 of 25 required rows: every completed row passed and matched the MTP0 final answer, but the twentieth request stopped at the repeated-session boundary and six rows did not run. MTP3 quality therefore remains inconclusive and unqualified, not failed. MTP1 active-1K and active-2K are separate no-output quarantines; the 2K request reached the client bound after partial prompt work, the engine then reported its own timeout, and no timing or quality credit is granted. MTP4 is the only exact-4K MTP-depth quarantine. Graph, vision, clean-host qualification, and deployment remain open

evidence.scope: exact TP4/EP4 eager MTP1 text serving at configured max 512 and configured max 4352 with a 32-block cache allocation, including active 4096-token context; configured max 1536 and 3072 are retained separately as bounded negatives
evidence.basis: The exact model, MTP adapter, preserved staged runtime, healthy API, all 26 MTP0 baseline comparisons, 16/16 repeat stability, cache-zero needles, complete usage, positive draft acceptance, short speed rows, and the exact-4K formal plus three-row deployment-shaped screen are retained. At 4K, the median was 8.904 tok/s decode, 232.1 seconds TTFT, and 0.981 tok/s wall output with 528/539 cumulative draft acceptance. Separate configured-1536 and configured-3072 boots passed admission but stopped during their first active-1K and active-2K requests without returning output tokens. The 2K client reached its 360-second bound with a zero-byte completion body; the subsequent engine diagnostic showed 448 computed prompt tokens and zero output, the engine reported its own timeout, and the post-failure teardown window recorded compute- and copy-class resets on all four cards before device rediscovery. Neither bounded negative grants performance timing or quality credit. The inherited target quality remains 5/7; the 32-block recipe is not a minimum-cache or causal cache claim, and vision, clean-boot replay, and deployment qualification remain missing. MTP3 remains the preferred exact-4K recipe.

1:2048.label: 360-second client timeout; 448 computed tokens; no output or speed
1:2048.reason: The exact 32-block configured-3072 identity passed all startup gates and exposed 7,561 cache tokens. Its first exact-2K exchange had a zero-byte completion body and no output token recorded when the fixed 360-second client bound expired; the subsequent engine diagnostic showed 448 computed prompt tokens and zero output, while vLLM completed-request, token, and MTP counters remained zero. The engine independently reported its own sampling timeout. Request two was not sent. The post-failure teardown window recorded compute- and copy-class resets on all four cards before all four were rediscovered; no post-reset collective was run. Existing MTP1 configured-512 and exact-4K passes and every captured speed remain unchanged.

Request two was not sent. The observed 4.527 tok/s is diagnostic only and does not alter the passing MTP2 512 or exact-4K results.
